lines: +      # Preserve the previous scope; newer goconst also checks composite literals.
- G104 # errors are handled at appropriate levels, checked by errcheck linter

+- **A private GitHub repository over 1.5 GiB now bootstraps in batches.** The GitHub repository-size lookup that selects batched bootstrap sent no credentials, so GitHub answered 404 for every private repository and the bootstrap silently sent the whole repository as one pack, whatever its size. The lookup now carries the source credentials, which also moves public lookups off the anonymous rate limit shared by everything behind the same IP; a token the API refuses (401/403) is retried once anonymously, so a public repository is never worse off. Each lookup's outcome (HTTP status or error, reported size, chosen mode) is now logged through `Options.BootstrapLogger` without verbose mode, at warning level when the size could not be determined, and a failed lookup prints a notice that the bootstrap stays a single pack. A `github.com` URL on a non-default port is no longer treated as GitHub, so its credentials never reach the GitHub API. ([#124](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/124))
+- Update the pinned Go toolchain to 1.27.2 to include the standard-library security fixes reported by `govulncheck`.

- Preserve source-read errors when closing bootstrap observation, including `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`; a truncated source is reported as `observer_failed`, not expected `observer_interrupted`. Intentional partial closure is unchanged. ([#120](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/120))

- At source EOF, bootstrap upload guards enforce actual bytes without projection or the batching safety margin. Final bytes returned together with EOF remain subject to the byte limit, and diagnostic counters retain their observed values. ([#120](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/120))
// BootstrapLogger receives one structured diagnostic per checkpoint upload,
-	// including failures, independently of verbose protocol logging. Nil disables
-	// these diagnostics. Bytes read are not proof of bytes accepted by the target.
+	// including failures, and one per GitHub repository-size lookup (warning
+	// level when the size could not be read), independently of verbose
+	// protocol logging. Nil disables these diagnostics. Bytes read are not
+	// proof of bytes accepted by the target.
// BootstrapFallbackMaxPackBytes bounds indivisible checkpoint uploads when
// the target has not announced a limit. Positive values disable projection

+A bootstrap from a `github.com` source that is not given `--target-max-pack-bytes` first asks the GitHub REST API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) for the repository size, sending the source credentials so a private repository answers too. When GitHub reports 1.5 GiB or more, the bootstrap switches to batches of 512 MiB (or `--max-pack-bytes`, if smaller). A token the API refuses (401 or 403) is retried once without credentials, which is enough for a public repository. When the lookup fails anyway — no credentials for a private repository, an exhausted rate limit, an unreachable API — the bootstrap stays a single pack and git-sync prints a notice saying so. The outcome, including the HTTP status or error, is logged with `-v` and through the library's `Options.BootstrapLogger`, at warning level when the lookup failed. Pass `--target-max-pack-bytes` to choose batching yourself and skip the lookup.
Batched bootstrap walks a chain of source commits and places sub-pack
them in your git credential helper against that host; git-sync will find them
+The GitHub repository-size lookup described under [Examples](#examples) follows
+the same rule: source credentials for `github.com` go to `api.github.com`, a
+subdomain on the same port, and to no other host. A `github.com` URL with a
+non-default port is not treated as GitHub, so it gets no lookup at all.

- Source-side discovery and fetch can use protocol v2 when supported. Push stays on the existing v1 `receive-pack` path. `--protocol auto` tries v2 first and falls back to v1. `--protocol v2` requires the source to negotiate v2.

file.content:
## Problem

When bootstrapping from a `github.com` source without `--target-max-pack-bytes`, git-sync asks the GitHub REST API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) for the repository size. It switches to 512 MiB batches when the size is 1.5 GiB or more. That lookup sent no credentials. For a private repository GitHub answers 404 to an anonymous caller, so every private repository bootstrapped as a single pack, whatever its size.

Nothing reported this:
- Every failure (non-200, transport error, parse error) returned silently.
- The "selected batched mode" message only showed with verbose logging.

Public repositories were exposed too: anonymous calls share GitHub's 60 requests/hour limit per egress IP.

## Changes

**Authenticated lookup**
- The size request now carries the source connection's credentials (basic or bearer).
- If the API refuses the token with 401 or 403 (for example an SSO-unauthorized PAT), the lookup retries once anonymously. A public repository is never worse off than before.
- Credentials go only to the GitHub API. `GitHubOwnerRepo` now treats `github.com` as GitHub only on its scheme's default port. The connection's redirect guard still strips credentials from any hop that leaves the API host.

**Visible outcome**
- Every lookup that is attempted is logged through `Options.BootstrapLogger`. This does not need verbose mode.
- Fields: `repository`, `authenticated`, `http_status`, `refused_auth_status`, `size_kb` or `error`, `threshold_kb`, `mode`, `target_max_pack_bytes`.
- A failed lookup logs at WARN and also prints a notice that the bootstrap stays a single pack, so CLI users see it without `-v`.

**Hardening**
- A reported size of 0 is treated as unknown: GitHub reports 0 until it has computed the size.
- The lookup has a 30s timeout.
- GitHub's error message is sanitized and truncated before it is logged.

**Docs**
- `docs/usage.md` documents the lookup and its credential scope.
- Updated the `BootstrapLogger` doc comments and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Tests

New file `internal/strategy/bootstrap/github_preflight_test.go`, written test-first. It covers:
- a private repo: 404 without auth, 200 with auth, so batched (also end-to-end through `Execute`);
- a bearer token;
- lookup failure: one-shot, a WARN record and a notice;
- the anonymous retry on 401/403, and no retry on other failures;
- a transport error, and unusable bodies (not JSON, no size, size 0);
- sanitizing GitHub's error message;
- a small repo staying one-shot;
- skipped lookups (caller already batching, non-default port, non-GitHub host);
- a redirect that leaves the API host dropping credentials.

The new tests fail against the previous implementation. `go test ./...`, `go test -race` on the affected packages and `golangci-lint run` (v2.11.4) all pass.

I updated the PR description: https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/124

- **Size 0:** the old "treated as unknown" line now says a size of 0 selects a single pack, logged at INFO with no warning or notice. A missing or negative size still counts as a failed lookup.
- **Token refusal:** the description says the refusal is reported when the anonymous retry also fails, lists the new `refused_auth_error` log field, and notes that the CLI notice names it.
- **Earlier commits:** it now covers two changes that came in after the description was written: tokens written into the source URL are sent, and `EndpointAuth` never hands over credentials looked up for a host a redirect led to.
- **Tests:** the list includes the new tests. I re-ran `go test -race` on the two affected packages and both pass, so the description's test claims still hold.

I didn't touch the Cursor Bugbot summary; the bot rewrites that section itself.

content.text:
Yes, mirror-pipeline can use this change in production without any code changes. The only step is to bump its git-sync dependency once #124 is merged.

**What I checked**
- **It builds and its tests pass against the PR branch.** I pointed a temporary workspace file at my local checkout of the PR branch (nothing in mirror-pipeline was modified). `go build ./...` and `go vet` pass, and every package's tests pass except one. That one is `TestGitSyncUserAgentIdentity`, and it fails only because a local checkout reports its version as `git-sync/dev`. It won't happen with a real version, and the same suite passes on mirror-pipeline's current pin. The installation-token leak guard (`TestSyncDoesNotLeakInstallationToken`) passes.
- **The worker actually runs the lookup.** The library never sets `TargetMaxPack`, sources are `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`, and requests to `api.github.com` go through the public transport, not the cluster mTLS one. entiredb-sourced syncs are not GitHub, so they skip the lookup.
- **The worker's token reaches the API.** The App token is passed as `Username: "x-access-token", Token: token`, which becomes explicit Basic auth on the source connection, and that is what the lookup sends.
- **GitHub's REST API accepts that form.** I checked live against the private `entirehq/mirror-pipeline` repo: anonymous gets 404, and Basic auth with `x-access-token:<token>` gets 200. I used my `gh` OAuth token, not an App installation token; the auth scheme is the same. Every GitHub App has repository metadata read, which is the only permission this call needs.
- **No regression for jobs without an installation ID.** They still look up anonymously, as before.

**What changes in production**
- Private GitHub repos of 1.5 GiB or more will now bootstrap in 512 MiB batches instead of one pack. This is the point of the fix, but it is new behaviour for those repos, so watch the first few large private bootstraps.
- Every bootstrap now writes a `Bootstrap GitHub size preflight` record through `BootstrapLogger`, carrying the worker's `target_ulid` and owner/repo fields. Failures log at WARN, so check whether any log monitor fires on WARN from mirror-worker.
- A failed lookup also prints one plain-text line to stderr. That's how git-sync's other notices already reach the library, but this one mentions the CLI flag `--target-max-pack-bytes`, which means nothing in the worker. The WARN record is the useful signal.
- Each bootstrap attempt makes one extra API call against the installation's rate limit, with at most 30 seconds of added wait.

**To ship:** after #124 merges, run `go get entire.io/entire/git-sync@<merge-sha>` in mirror-pipeline. The PR is based on the commit mirror-pipeline already pins (`013012ac`), so nothing else comes with it.

content.text:
The review found no crash bugs, but it did find three real problems with where credentials can end up. None of them affect mirror-pipeline, which passes an explicit App token, keeps TLS verification on and uses no credential helper. The review ran at xhigh, not high: it reuses the last level and didn't pick up the `high` I passed. I checked #2 against the code myself.

**Credential handling (should fix)**
1. **`EndpointAuth` checks the wrong host pair** (`smarthttp.go:495`). It asks whether the host the helper credentials were looked up for is on the endpoint's site. It never asks whether the host they're sent to may receive them. Example: a redirect to `replica.github.com` makes the helper return that host's credentials, and the lookup then sends them to `api.github.com`, which is a sibling of that host, not a subdomain. This needs redirect-following plus a helper entry for the replica host, so it's an edge case, but it breaks the rule the `samesite.go` comment claims.
2. **Credentials go out with TLS verification off** (`bootstrap.go:1936`). `HTTPConn` already refuses to send helper credentials to another host when TLS verification is skipped (`skipsTLSVerify`, lines 790 and 891), but the lookup bypasses that check. With verification off, anyone who can intercept `api.github.com` gets the github.com token. Explicit tokens go out the same way.
3. **The rate-limit claim is overstated.** The credential helper is only asked after a 401, and a public repo never returns one, so its lookup stays anonymous. The changelog and `usage.md` promise rate-limit relief that only applies to `--source-token` or tokens written into the URL.

**My earlier nit fix was wrong**
5. **A bare username is now sent as a credential** (`bootstrap.go:1939`). `https://alice@github.com/...` or `git@` goes to the API as Basic `alice:`. GitHub answers 401, which costs a wasted request, may count as a failed login, and logs a misleading refusal. The code can't tell a token written as the username from an account name. I'd revert to requiring a password.

**Logging and accuracy (minor)**
4. The failure notice says "bootstrapping as a single pack", but the run can still switch to batches if the target rejects the pack. It also names a CLI flag that library callers don't have, and with `-v` the failure prints twice.
6. `authenticated: true` is set when credentials are attached, even if a redirect stripped them before they arrived.
7. The comment says control characters are stripped from GitHub's message, but `sanitize.Text` only filters single bytes. Two-byte control characters such as U+009B and bidi overrides still reach the terminal.
8. `TestGitHubPreflightRedirectDropsCredentials` also passes if the redirect target is never contacted. It should assert that the target received exactly one request.

**Design**
9. The policy for which credentials may go to a sibling service is split between `gitproto.EndpointAuth` and `bootstrap.sourceCredentials`, and neither checks the real destination. One method such as `HTTPConn.CredentialsFor(dest)`, applying `sameSite(origin, dest)` and the TLS check to every credential source, would fix #1, #2 and #5 together.
10. `githubSizeLookup` stores state it could derive. The two log messages also use different names (`bootstrap github preflight` vs `Bootstrap GitHub size preflight`), so a query for one misses the other.

I'd fix #9 (which also covers #1, #2 and #5), correct the docs for #3, and do #4, #6, #7 and #8 while I'm there. Should I go ahead?

40:A bootstrap from a `github.com` source that is not given `--target-max-pack-bytes` first asks the GitHub REST API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`) for the repository size, sending the source credentials so a private repository answers too. When GitHub reports 1.5 GiB or more, the bootstrap switches to batches of 512 MiB (or `--max-pack-bytes`, if smaller). A token the API refuses (401 or 403) is retried once without credentials, which is enough for a public repository. When the lookup fails anyway — no credentials for a private repository, an exhausted rate limit, an unreachable API — the bootstrap stays a single pack and git-sync prints a notice saying so. The outcome, including the HTTP status or error, is logged with `-v` and through the library's `Options.BootstrapLogger`, at warning level when the lookup failed. Pass `--target-max-pack-bytes` to choose batching yourself and skip the lookup.

44-Batched bootstrap walks a chain of source commits and places sub-pack
45-boundaries (checkpoints) along it, so each push fits under

398:The GitHub repository-size lookup described under [Examples](#examples) follows
399-the same rule: source credentials for `github.com` go to `api.github.com`, a
400-subdomain on the same port, and to no other host. A `github.com` URL with a
401-non-default port is not treated as GitHub, so it gets no lookup at all.

403-## Protocol Notes
32:- **A private GitHub repository over 1.5 GiB now bootstraps in batches.** The GitHub repository-size lookup that selects batched bootstrap sent no credentials, so GitHub answered 404 for every private repository and the bootstrap silently sent the whole repository as one pack, whatever its size. The lookup now carries the source credentials, which also moves public lookups off the anonymous rate limit shared by everything behind the same IP; a token the API refuses (401/403) is retried once anonymously, so a public repository is never worse off, and the refusal is reported if the retry fails too. Each lookup's outcome (HTTP status or error, reported size, chosen mode) is now logged through `Options.BootstrapLogger` without verbose mode, at warning level when the size could not be determined, and a failed lookup prints a notice that the bootstrap stays a single pack. A `github.com` URL on a non-default port is no longer treated as GitHub, so its credentials never reach the GitHub API. ([#124](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/124))

"""for the repository size, sending the source credentials so a private repository answers too. A token the API refuses (401 or 403) is retried once without credentials, which is enough for a public repository. The outcome, including the HTTP status or error, is logged with `-v` and through the library's `Options.BootstrapLogger`, at warning level when the lookup failed.""",
"""for the repository size. It sends the source credentials git-sync holds at that point, so a private repository answers too: a `--source-token`, a `user:token@` in the source URL, or credentials the git credential helper supplied when the git server asked for them. A public repository never asks, so with only a credential helper its lookup stays anonymous and counts against GitHub's anonymous rate limit. When GitHub reports 1.5 GiB or more, the bootstrap switches to batches of 512 MiB (or `--max-pack-bytes`, if smaller); a reported size of 0 (an empty repository, or one GitHub has not sized yet) keeps a single pack. A token the API refuses (401 or 403) is retried once without credentials, which is enough for a public repository. When the lookup fails anyway — no credentials for a private repository, an exhausted rate limit, an unreachable API — the bootstrap starts with a single pack and git-sync prints a notice naming the cause, including the refusal when a token was refused first. The bootstrap can still switch to batches later if the target rejects the pack as too large. The outcome, including the HTTP status or error, goes to the library's `Options.BootstrapLogger`, at warning level when the lookup failed, and a successful lookup is also logged with `-v`.""")

edit('docs/usage.md',
"""the same rule: source credentials for `github.com` go to `api.github.com`, a
subdomain on the same port, and to no other host. A `github.com` URL with a
non-default port is not treated as GitHub, so it gets no lookup at all.""",

credentials for `github.com` go to `api.github.com`, a subdomain on the same
port, and to no other host. Credentials the helper looked up for a host a
redirect led to stay with that host, and with TLS verification off no
credential is sent to the API at all. A `github.com` URL with a non-default
